newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CBA says volumes offset margin fall.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CBA says volumes offset margin fall.

text.p: Commonwealth Bank of Australia (CBA) said on Wednesday that increased lending volumes more than offset a fall in the group's interest margins.

CBA increased lending volumes in the six months to December 31 by 14 percent to a total of A$86.65 billion, while the group's interest margin fell to 3.71 percent from 4.12 percent on June 30 last year.
Australian interest margins fell to 4.06 percent from 4.5 percent at June 30, while the overseas interest margin fell to 2.16 percent from 2.39 percent.

"The result reflects continuing cost containment, with the cost-to-income ratio falling from 60.9 percent to 60.3 percent," the bank said in a detailed financial summary of its latest half year profit result.
"Excluding the impact of the buyback on earnings the cost-to-income ratio would have been 59.5 percent," it said.
Staff productivity rose by three percent.
Commercial lending approvals increased by 33 percent over the half year to December 31 with balances outstanding increasing by eight percent.
New equipment finance increased by 30 percent.
CBA said its charge for bad and doubtful debts fell to A$43 million, down 25 percent on the A$57 million recorded in the first half of 1995/96.
The bank's underlying profit, which exclude bad debt charges, income tax, and outside equity interests, rose six percent to A$980 million from A$924 million.

CBA said its total risk-weighted capital ratio fell to 10.94 percent from 12.15 percent at December 31, 1995, and from 12.71 percent at June 30 last year. Its tier one risk weighted capital ratio fell to 8.72 percent from 10.05 percent on June 30.
